headline: Validity checks expose inflated false positives in association and replication analyses
label: Association Analysis Validity Testing
summary: Growing association datasets demand explicit tests of false-positive control and cross-cohort replication before biological interpretation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is whether apparent associations survive explicit validity checks. In synthetic and 14 brain datasets, surrogate variable analysis inflates false positives and lowers cross-cohort reproducibility. ScreenDMT extends the directional MaxP test to multi-study replication, with proven FDR validity supported by simulations, and is applied to blood-based metabolite data across three cohorts in sleep disorders. A biobank G×E analysis shows that power and log transformation of the phenotype scale explain 45% and 23% of PGS×sex interactions, so scale choice can generate apparent interactions. The Multi-scale Copula Index is an association measure that avoids density estimation and tuning, with benchmarks extending to cancer genomics. A gradient-boosting Meniere disease classifier (test AUC 0.843) is a predictive application rather than an inferential one. What is new is framing each method around a defined validity question, such as false-positive control, replication, or phenotype-scale artefact, rather than general performance alone.
